questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a country that I hadn't visited before and Australia/Oceania was an area that I had been on my bucket list for a long time. I also wanted to study at a university that could offer me academic challenges and courses in a specific field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a lot easier than in Nordic countries. The university offered multiple different orientation events and help was easy to find. During the orientation week, multiple companies came to the university to offer help with setting up a bank account, free sim cards, travel cards, etc. They also had specific people to only help students with their matters the whole semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mostly the ones described before. Also, other students and my flatmates were helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think they offered more than enough assistance and it was easy to reach. Never felt like I was alone with my problems.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy, I was able to find my first room within just a few days after arrival. I used Facebook groups, Facebook marketplace, and an app called flatmates for finding a room in a shared house. I moved houses one time during my stay because I was unsatisfied with my first share house.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be relatively cheaper to live off campus, but student dorms are a great way of meeting new people. Australia's rental markets work on a weekly basis instead of monthly. That means that new rooms come available all the time and there is quite a lot to choose from. However, the quality of housing is lower in relation to the price you pay but that applies to all housing. It is quite common to not have rental contracts.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: On-campus housing is very expensive and the quality is bad. One dorm was very moldy and some people got very sick after living there for a couple of weeks.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration for courses was relatively easy and it was done online. I was able to change one course on the second week of the semester and that was easy too. The university offered help if you had any problems and they responded quickly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above they had specific people just to help students with registration and other issues. You could email or call them, or visit them on campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted. I changed one of my courses in the second week because it wasn't what I was expecting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Spend time looking into the courses but don't stress too much because changing them is relatively easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was positively surprised by the academic program at my host university. Even though studying was a lot more work than at KU, the quality of teaching was high and the student community was helpful.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Each course required more work than in KU. I studied full-time which meant 4 units. I had weekly readings of approximately 300 pages, weekly quizzes and multiple graded assignments during the semester. However, I don't think they were very harsh on grading since it was quite easy to get good grades. I think you would be able to set the bar low if you wanted.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think the biggest difference was that there were more graded assignments and weekly quizzes on the lectures and readings. They were very clear about what they are expecting from students. In some classes, we had more seminar-type of discussions and others were more like lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: PICT8040 Cyber crime and policy, PICT8037 Pathways into terrorism, PICT8044 Intelligence analysis, PICT8062 Crimes of the powerful

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you're interested in criminology and security studies/intelligence, I would recommend all of these courses. I especially loved the one in cybercrime. They have a very nice selection of courses in this field. I recommend participating in class even though they offer the possibility to study online.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Overseas healthcare does not cover all the fees, you still have to pay a bit yourself.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Covid -19 self-tests and masks were more expensive than in Europe. Eating out was cheaper than I expected. Fresh vegetables were very expensive in winter. In general, I'd say that living was cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They offered multiple different clubs and organizations at the uni. However, some of them never organized any meetups. The exchange student society only organized one event during the semester and it was during the exam period. The uni has a new gym and pool but they were not very cheap. In general, joining sports clubs was a bit expensive and some of them didn't take new members this semester.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a wide selection of societies that offer different activities based on nationality (i.e., Nordic society), religion (i.e., Christian groups), and other interests such as parties, music, and different sports (climbing, volleyball, dancing)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't really participate in the non-academic activities but probably any of them could be nice depending on what your interests are.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Sydney is such a cool city and there is so much to do and discover! There are so many nice restaurants to eat in, Parramatta is a cool Indian district, visit the markets in Glebe and the Rocks, hang out in Manly, transport using the ferries, and go hiking in the many national parks surrounding Sydney. Also, travel a lot of course. I visited New Zealand during the two weeks mid-semester break and it was amazing! It was relatively easy to travel during the semester even when I had classes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Australians are relatively easy-going so it wasn't too hard to adjust. Practical things like setting up a bank account and getting a sim card were very easy. They are not very big on writing contracts for jobs or housing, so you have to be careful. The weekly system was weird at first. And don't underestimate the Australian winter, it gets cold.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to meet people in the class, they are very international and more talkative. Joining clubs and events would be another good way to meet local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The weekly system, unwillingness to write contracts, and quality of housing. They don't have as many vegetarian options available as in Europe.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are quite easy-going, they have a lot of cultural events going on in Sydney, and many museums and galleries are free. The food is amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: If you decide to live off campus, take your time with finding a room in an area you like. Bring warm clothes if you come for session 2, it was cold in July! Get mentally prepared to study, the session was intense (only 13 weeks of studying). But the campus is very nice with loads of green areas, cool study spots, and food options.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though the quality of housing is lower you can find very nice houses to live in with a good location. If you wish to work beside your studies, it is easy to find a job in a cafe or a restaurant.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got many chances to travel in Australia and see beautiful places. I really enjoyed my units and the teaching at my host university. I feel like I found a new perspective on my studies at KU.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't know if I had very great challenges but the weather when I arrived really surprised me (it was cold) and I didn't have enough warm clothing. The studying was quite tough especially when I didn't have a proper break between the semesters here and at KU.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would 100% recommend Macquarie University to anyone wanting to go to Australia. Even though the campus is a bit far from the center, the public transportation is good and the campus is very cool.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
